Within the government, the main
reference center for unidentified
flying objects is located in the Ministry of Aeronautics, in the Core of the Brazilian Aerospace Defense Command, known by the acronym Nucomdabra.
The way this core operates is the subject of much debate. UFOlogists swear that Nucomdabra investigates UFO appearances, dispatches agents to locations where they may have appeared, and monitors Brazilian airspace for suspicious movements.
The Aeronautics denies it. "What we do is receive information and archive, archive, archive. Why don't we investigate? Because there is no specific directive in that sense," says Brigadier José Montgomeri Rebouças, head of the Social Communication Center of the Ministry of Aeronautics.
"It must be a fascinating topic because we receive a lot of information, but we do not give scientific treatment to these reports, nor do we consider flying saucers as an aerial threat," he says.

Andrade also sent a standard questionnaire, requesting a series of information about the UFO, such as "the object's position," its shape, size, color, speed and trail, trajectory, and duration of observation.

The Brazilian military regime
(1964-1985) investigated, in the
1970s, cases of alleged UFO sightings and spied on the activities of Brazilian specialists in ET (extraterrestrials).
Documents from the former Dops
(Department of Political and Social Order), now stored in the State Archive of São Paulo, show that the so-called intelligence services wasted time and money investigating the "abduction" of a Paulista merchant by crewmembers of an Unidentified Flying Object (UFO).
The documents also show that Dops even called two ufologists, people who study UFOs, to testify and infiltrated an agent to attend periodic meetings of a group of UFO enthusiasts.
Located by historian Cláudio Tsuyoshi Suenaga, the documents confirm something that Brazilian ufologists have always suspected, but that the scientific community only saw as another symptom of the obsession that afflicts many of these scholars: "The military always worried about the UFO phenomenon," says Suenaga.
"X-Files"
The historian, who is preparing a master's thesis on the subject at Unesp (State University of Paulista), goes further: "It's clear that there is a Brazilian 'X-Files'. Even today, there is concern by the Brazilian government on this topic."
Suenaga is referring to the popular American science fiction series "X-Files," broadcast on TV.
The program tells the story of the investigation of unexplained cases (UFOs, ET, paranormal, etc), archived (423 km northwest of São Paulo).
His report was sent to Romeu Tuma, the police chief, who then forwarded it to the then director-general of Dops.
The agent, disguised, attended a meeting of ufologists on April 27, 1975, and reported details of the encounter near Guarantã.
The delegate rushed to identify the participants and asked the Dops to investigate, under the rubric "X-Files."
Believing People

In January 1975, the investigation was closed, with no conclusion drawn about the veracity of the encounter.

Located off Highway DF 001, at kilometer 4, is DF 465, the access road to the security area of the Papuda Prison. At approximately 1.5 kilometers southeast of Brasília's Plano Piloto, it is situated in a valley with a symmetrical altitude of 990 meters on average. Surrounding areas have elevations ranging from 1,150 meters.

Within the security area: the Internment and Reintegration Center (CIR), which housed around 700 prisoners with sentences ranging from 10 to 15 years in April 1991, the Brasília Custody Core (NCB), under the responsibility of the District Federal Civil Police, housing around 400 prisoners awaiting trial, and the 3rd Independent Military Company (3ª CPVtlnd), whose guard corps consisted of over 60 men.

It is a secluded area from the urban center. Most of its area has no significance. Inside the maximum-security prison, CIR, surveillance is done with 10 high-powered floodlights. It has 10 guard towers for superior surveillance and ground guard posts.

On the night of April 11, 1991, from 7:10 pm to 10:40 pm, an Unidentified Flying Object (UFO) was observed by Sergeant Damasceno and the soldiers on guard that night. Approximately 25 police officers were present at the 3rd CPMInd. The rest of the guard force, comprising the night watch, were spread out on other missions and guard posts.

What was observed:

Lieutenant Damasceno left the 3rd CPMInd and ordered Sergeant Reinaldo to prepare the vehicle for a patrol around the prison posts, a routine procedure. Upon returning to the company, he noticed a strange object about 300-400 meters high in the sky. He immediately called the guard to see it, with around 20 police officers present at that moment.

According to testimonies, the object constantly changed colors: blue, red, yellow, and a bit of green, occasionally blinking intensely, turning the entire object red. Observations were made from three different positions within the security perimeter, and there were also reports of other witnesses. We verified that these were individuals providing services at nearby charcoal kilns.

In the week following the collection of testimonies, we traveled to the charcoal kiln region. The service provision system, with high turnover, did not allow us to contact all witnesses.

Initially, I would like to express my highest regards and consideration, taking the opportunity to commend the work done with dedication and zeal.

Despite containing already known accounts regarding the so-called "Operation Plate" in the Amazon, these are stamped and endorsed by the mission chief, who stated it resulted in over 500 photographs and 4 films, 3 of which purchased by then-Captain Hollanda himself.

Adding to the impressive accounts are pages and pages of mission reports, complete with maps, sketches, and testimonies of all sorts of occurrences involving unidentified flying objects (UFOs) in the lower Brazilian airspace, which brought great fear to that population due to the consequences of such phenomena.

I recall the incident with the Tucano plane from the "Fumaça Squadron" in Santos, where amateur yet real films show an unknown aerial form at the time of the accident. For me, this raises a question for which I do not see a plausible answer, or by denying the facts, aren't we in a way fueling unnecessary speculations?

Furthermore, knowing that the UFO subject arouses scorn in the population, with those who believe in them being labeled as lunatics, why hide or rather, refuse to disclose documents, at least to those who seek them, whether they are ufologists or not, since no one else will believe, and the opinion will be that it's just the ramblings of a lunatic and will end there. Never will the FAB. the COMD AB RA, or the Ministry of Aeronautics, suffer any damage to their images, as for the majority of the Brazilian population, UFOs are a farcical matter.

Under no circumstances do I intend to disrespect opinions, but access to the photographs and films mentioned by Colonel Hollanda would bring great relief to those interested in the subject.

When I heard Colonel Hollanda describing a UFO sighted near Belém, I visualized films made around the world, such as in Mexico-Miami, Germany, showing the same UFO model, where cameramen did not know each other and never believed in UFOs. Indeed, in March 1996, in Duque de Caxias, Rio de Janeiro, a film showing this model was taken by a cameraman filming a lunar eclipse.

Therefore, the description of the UFO sighted by Colonel Hollanda is completely consistent with these others captured at different times, in different cities, in different countries.
